q-95010.name: Question 1
q-95010.problem:
$$
{A}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}],\,{A}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}9 & 4 \\ -5 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices shown above. Find the matrix $C$ given that $B=\{{A}_{1},{A}_{2}\}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}\{{A}_{1},{A}_{2}\},$ and the coordinates of the matrix $C$ relative to $B$ are $[C]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$
q-95010.worked_solution:
Any vector in $\text{Span}\{{A}_{1},{A}_{2}\}$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{A}_{1}+{x}_{2}{A}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
[C]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}C & =4\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]+(-1)\cdot [\begin{aligned}9 & 4 \\ -5 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -4 \\ 0 & 12\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-9 & -4 \\ 5 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & -8 \\ 5 & 9\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1

A1=[1−103],A2=[94−53]

Consider the matrices shown above. Find the matrix C given that B={A1,A2} is a basis of Span{A1,A2}, and the coordinates of the matrix C relative to B are [C]B=[4−1].

a
C=[−13−85−15]
b
C=[5059]
c
C=[−5−8−5−9]
d
C=[−50−515]
e
C=[−5−859]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Any vector in Span{A1,A2} can be written as

x1A1+x2A2.

In our case, we have

[C]B=[x1x2]=[4−1].

Therefore, C=4⋅[1−103]+(−1)⋅[94−53]=[4−4012]+[−9−45−3]=[−5−859].

q-36476.name: Question 2
q-36476.problem:
$$
{A}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 2 & -3\end{aligned}],\,{A}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 5 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices shown above. Find the matrix $C$ given that $B=\{{A}_{1},{A}_{2}\}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}\{{A}_{1},{A}_{2}\},$ and the coordinates of the matrix $C$ relative to $B$ are $[C]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3\end{aligned}].$
q-36476.worked_solution:
Any vector in $\text{Span}\{{A}_{1},{A}_{2}\}$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{A}_{1}+{x}_{2}{A}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
[C]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}C & =2\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 2 & -3\end{aligned}]+(-3)\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 5 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 4 & -6\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ -15 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ -11 & -6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

q-106738.name: Question 3
q-106738.problem:
Consider the polynomials ${p}_{1}(t)$ and ${p}_{2}(t),$ given by

$$
{p}_{1}(t)=1+t+{t}^{2},\,{p}_{2}(t)=1+t-{t}^{2}.
$$

Find $p(t)$ given that $B=\{{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)\}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}\{{p}_{1},{p}_{2}\},$ and the coordinates of $p(t)$ relative to $B$ are $[p(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$
q-106738.worked_solution:
Any vector in  $\text{Span}\{{p}_{1},{p}_{2}\}$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}{p}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
[p(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}p(t) & =(-1)\cdot (1+t+{t}^{2})+1\cdot (1+t-{t}^{2}) \\  & =-1-t-{t}^{2}+1+t-{t}^{2} \\  & =-2{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-95007.html:
Question 4
?

Consider the polynomials p1(t) and p2(t), given by p1(t)=t−t3,p2(t)=2t2+5t3. Find p(t) given that B={p1(t),p2(t)} is a basis of Span{p1,p2}, and the coordinates of p(t) relative to B are [p(t)]B=[−31].

a
p(t)=−3t+2t2+8t3
b
p(t)=−t2+4t3
c
p(t)=−3t+2t2−2t3
d
p(t)=3t+2t2−2t3
e
p(t)=3t+6t3
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Any vector in Span{p1,p2} can be written as

x1p1(t)+x2p2(t).

In our case, we have

[p(t)]B=[x1x2]=[−31].

Therefore,

p(t)=(−3)⋅(t−t3)+1⋅(2t2+5t3)=−3t+3t3+2t2+5t3=−3t+2t2+8t3.

q-95003.name: Question 5
q-95003.problem:
Consider the polynomials ${p}_{1}(t)$ and ${p}_{2}(t),$ given by

$$
{p}_{1}(t)=1-t+2{t}^{2},\,{p}_{2}(t)=t-{t}^{2}.
$$

Find $p(t)$ given that $B=\{{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)\}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}\{{p}_{1},{p}_{2}\},$ and the coordinates of $p(t)$ relative to $B$ are $[p(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$
q-95003.worked_solution:
Any vector in  $\text{Span}\{{p}_{1},{p}_{2}\}$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}{p}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
[p(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}p(t) & =1\cdot (1-t+2{t}^{2})+3\cdot (t-{t}^{2}) \\  & =1-t+2{t}^{2}+3t-3{t}^{2} \\  & =1+2t-{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

Consider the polynomials p1(t) and p2(t), given by p1(t)=1−t+2t2,p2(t)=t−t2. Find p(t) given that B={p1(t),p2(t)} is a basis of Span{p1,p2}, and the coordinates of p(t) relative to B are [p(t)]B=[13].

a
p(t)=1+2t−6t2
b
p(t)=1+4t−t2
c
p(t)=1+2t−5t2
d
p(t)=1−3t−t2
e
p(t)=1+2t−t2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Any vector in Span{p1,p2} can be written as

x1p1(t)+x2p2(t).

In our case, we have

[p(t)]B=[x1x2]=[13].

Therefore,

p(t)=1⋅(1−t+2t2)+3⋅(t−t2)=1−t+2t2+3t−3t2=1+2t−t2.

q-95012.problem:
Consider the following matrices:

$$
{B}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}0 & 6 \\ 9 & 7\end{aligned}],\,{B}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 1 & 8\end{aligned}],\,A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ -7 & 9\end{aligned}]
$$

If $B=\{{B}_{1},{B}_{2}\}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}\{{B}_{1},{B}_{2}\},$ and $[A]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],$ then ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=$
q-95012.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{B}_{1}+{x}_{2}{B}_{2}=A.
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}0 & 6 \\ 9 & 7\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 1 & 8\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ -7 & 9\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & 6{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} \\ 9{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} & 7{x}_{1}+8{x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ -7 & 9\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding entries, we obtain

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{2}=2 \\ 6{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}=4 \\ 9{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-7 \\ 7{x}_{1}+8{x}_{2}=9.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 2 \\ 6 & 5 & 4 \\ 9 & 1 & -7 \\ 7 & 8 & 9\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 2 \\ 6 & 5 & 4 \\ 9 & 1 & -7 \\ 7 & 8 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}↔{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}6 & 5 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 9 & 1 & -7 \\ 7 & 8 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-\frac{3}{2}){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+(-\frac{7}{6}){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}6 & 5 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & -\frac{13}{2} & -13 \\ 0 & \frac{13}{6} & \frac{13}{3}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}6{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}=4 \\ {x}_{2}=2 \\ -\frac{13}{2}{x}_{2}=-13 \\ \frac{13}{6}{x}_{2}=\frac{13}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second, third and fourth equations, we get ${x}_{2}=2.$ From the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}6{x}_{1}+5\cdot 2 & =4 \\ 6{x}_{1} & =-6 \\ {x}_{1} & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, $[A]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-1+2=1.$

$$
{x}_{1}{B}_{1}+{x}_{2}{B}_{2}=A.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}5 & -3 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -3 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} & -3{x}_{2} \\ 0 & -2{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -3 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding entries, we obtain

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}=4 \\ -3{x}_{2}=-3 \\ -2{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=5.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & 5 & 4 \\ 0 & -3 & -3 \\ -2 & 4 & 5\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}2 & 5 & 4 \\ 0 & -3 & -3 \\ -2 & 4 & 5\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}2 & 5 & 4 \\ 0 & -3 & -3 \\ 0 & 9 & 9\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}=4 \\ -3{x}_{2}=-3 \\ 9{x}_{2}=9.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second and third equations, we get ${x}_{2}=1.$ From the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+5\cdot 1 & =4 \\ 2{x}_{1} & =-1 \\ {x}_{1} & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}

$$

$$

Equating the coefficients of $t$, we obtain

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{3}=-2 \\ 2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=4 \\ {x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=3 \\ -2{x}_{1}-6{x}_{2}=-6.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 2 & 1 & 3 & 4 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 & 3 \\ -2 & -6 & 0 & -6\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 2 & 1 & 3 & 4 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 & 3 \\ -2 & -6 & 0 & -6\end{aligned}] &  & {R}_{1}↔{R}_{3} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -2 \\ -2 & -6 & 0 & -6\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & -5 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=3 \\ -5{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=-2 \\ -2{x}_{3}=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=1.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$

$$
